english: Two gods made a pledge. This one shall give cattle, and that one shall give a horse. Then this one gave the cattle, and that one seized them. Then this one cried out: "Where is my horse?" Then that one said: "I did not seize your cattle. Dyeus knows my pledge. If I deceive you, may Dyeus strike me down." Then Dyeus heard him and thundered. Then that one became afraid and gave the horse to this one. Dyeus is the witness (the one who knows) of the pledge.

english: A man was ploughing the field with a plough. Then he grew tired and sat down. Then the Mother appeared to him and said: "Man, you are ploughing me with the plough. I nourish you and your cattle. If you give me a gift, I will give you grain." Then the man asked: "What shall I give you?" Then she said: "Give me seed." Then the man put the seed in the earth, and she gave him much grain. The grain grew. Then the man was making a hymn for her.

english: The gods were going to the father, and the son of Dyeus (of the sky) stood up and called on the father: "Father Dyeus, I have no name. Give me a name." Then Dawn spoke: "Let his name be 'Swift'." Then the father said: "He is my son, and men shall hear his name." Then he gave him a famous name, and the gods rejoiced. His name is famous, and his fame is imperishable.

english: The Swift god was stealing the cattle of Dyeus at night, and he drove them to a field. Then he drove them into the river, and the cattle swam. Then he hid them in a marsh. An old man was sitting at the door. The old man had sharp ears. Then he saw the god and recognized him. Then Dyeus was looking at dawn for his own cattle, and he did not see them. Then he called the old man: "Who took my cattle?" Then the old man said: "The god took them. I saw him." Then the father was saying: "Swift god, you were stealing my cattle. Bring them back." Then the Swift god became afraid, brought the cattle back, and gave two bulls. "Father, do not strike me." Then the father said: "Live, and do not steal again."

Then the Wind said: "I carry the clouds and the breath of men." Then the father said: "I have heard your word. Let the clouds be your swift horses; yoke them." Then the Wind yoked the clouds and drove them on. Then Dawn and the Wind went together, and men saw them. The clouds ran, and the thunder roared.

Then it said: "Dawn, daughter of Dyeus, I hear you. Where shall I go, and what shall I do?" Then Dawn said: "Go up, and look at the village and the path. Men are lying down." Then Perkunos was lifting the wheel, and he was not able. Then Fire grasped it, and the wheel was heavy. Then Dawn stood up, lifted the wheel, and carried it up. Then the father said: "Dawn, daughter of Dyeus, you have lifted the wheel. I will give you a good gift." Dawn carries it up, and men see her.

Then it (the Sun) said: "I am great, and I warm men. Who is able?" (Then:) "Wind, blow! If the man lets go of the garment, you have won." Then the Wind blew three times, and he kept holding his own garment. Then the man trembled. Then it (the Sun) warmed him, and he sweated and let go of the garment. Then the Sun won.

Then a man cried out: "Mother, what shall we sow in the field?" Then she said: "Sow seed and grain. Sow into it (the field)." Then the people heard the mother and went to it (the field). english: It was getting dark. Then the gods arrived, and the father seated them. Then Fire stood up and cried out: "Father Dyeus, hear me: when I burn in the hearth, Water comes and kills me." Then Water said: "I am not seeking you. You are seeking me." Then he said: "Fire, sit down in the hearth; and Water, go to the rivers, and do not come to the hearth." Then he (Fire) sat down in the hearth, and Water went to the rivers. Fire lives in the hearth, and Water lives in the rivers. Fire warms the people, and water gives the people drink.

It rained. Then the gods arrived together, and the father was sitting above. Then Mother Earth stood up and called on Dyeus: "Father, hear me, and dear gods, listen. Men, cattle, and sheep are heavy upon me. My heart is heavy, and I have grown weary. Who will lift these men off me?" Then he said to her: "Mother, I have heard your word. The old shall die and lie down in the earth. Then you will not be heavy. May the gods give you rest." Then they heard his word and rejoiced. Then she sat down in peace. Death comes to the old, and she protects them. Men give her gifts in spring.

english: A lady was walking on the path and weeping. Her husband had died, and her tears were falling. Then it dawned, and Dawn came forth to her. Then the lady was looking at her and calling on her: "Dawn, daughter of Dyeus, hear me. My husband has died. What shall I do?" Then Dawn said: "Lady, do not weep. I have heard you. Death comes to men, but fame does not die. I will give you a son. He will be of good fame, and his might will be great." Then the lady asked: "What shall I give you?" Then Dawn said: "Give me a hymn." Then the lady made a hymn for Dawn and offered her a gift. Then Dawn vanished. Within the year a son came to her. His name was famous.

english: An old man and his wife lived by the path. The wife was cooking grain. It rained, and a stranger came at night. Then the old man said: "Guest, sit down. Eat cooked grain. Drink water. I have a ram. I will kill it." Then the stranger said: "Do not kill the ram. I am not a stranger. I am a god. Old man, you gave me cooked grain and water. I will give you much livestock, and I will give you good fame. May your lifespan grow long." Then the stranger vanished. Then the old man saw livestock in the field, and the wife rejoiced.

Then he asked: "Where is the village?" Then she said: "The village is over there." Then the man followed her and reached the village. Then the man gave worship to the Moon and rejoiced.

Whoever does not give a gift to the gods, his boat shall sink." Then the wind blew, and the lake grew rough. Then the boat sank, the king died, and men did not invoke his name.
